text:
Kent Johnson is the one Blue Jacket whose season is going right. He has 19 points in 19 games, a point a game after 22 points in 76 last season, and our numbers flag it as a breakout: his ice time is up from 13:14 to 18:14, and he's on the ice for 80% of Columbus's power-play chances after 37% last year.

It's more than opportunity. His own chances are up to 0.97 expected goals per 60 from 0.69, and he ranks 15th of 542 skaters in our wins added, meaning his goals have come when they swung games. Eight goals on 5.6 expected says the finishing is running hot, and 19 games is a small sample. Ice time settles faster than scoring does.

The context matters too. Columbus is winless in five, and with Sean Monahan out Johnson's minutes have climbed again (20:43 a night over the last two games). Last season Evolving-Hockey had the team creating less with him on the ice. This season it's roughly even, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says half his shots come off the rush. He's become a player the Blue Jackets need, not just one they're developing.
